content: 1. Idelalisib affects the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which can alter its levels or effects. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, monitor for signs of idelalisib toxicity and adjust the dosage as needed if adverse reactions occur. 2. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. As idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor, avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 3. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of idelalisib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, monitor for idelalisib toxicity and adjust the dosage if adverse reactions occur. 4. Lopinavir decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir also decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Ritonavir increases the effects of ifosfamide by affecting CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration of ifosfamide with CYP2B6 inducers may increase its metabolism to active metabolites. Monitor for increased effects or toxicities. 6. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by affecting both CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Iloperidone increases ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Iloperidone increases lopinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A4. Monitor closely. 8. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of imatinib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Lopinavir also increases imatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. 9. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of imipramine by affecting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Lopinavir and ritonavir may increase the QTc interval when coadministered with inhaled indacaterol. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir increases indacaterol levels by modulating P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 activities. No dose adjustment is needed at the 75 mcg dose, but monitor closely. 11. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of indinavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Indinavir and ritonavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Indinavir also increases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Lopinavir increases indinavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. 12. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of infibratinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Lopinavir also increases infibratinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. 13. Lopinavir and inotuzumab both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs and monitor electrolytes before and after initiation of QTc-prolonging drugs. 14. Ritonavir decreases the effects of insulin aspart due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. Lopinavir has a similar effect. Reports indicate hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. 15. Ritonavir decreases the effects of insulin degludec via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. HIV protease inhibitors may cause new-onset diabetes mellitus, exacerbate existing diabetes, and induce hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. 16. Ritonavir decreases the effects of insulin detemir, insulin glargine, insulin glulisine, and insulin lispro due to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor closely. Lopinavir has similar effects. Reports indicate hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. 17. Ritonavir decreases the effects of inhaled insulin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. HIV protease inhibitors may cause new-onset diabetes mellitus, exacerbate existing diabetes, and induce hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. 18. Ritonavir decreases the effects of regular human insulin and insulin NPH due to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor closely. Lopinavir has similar effects. Reports indicate hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. 19. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of irinotecan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir increases irinotecan levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. Lopinavir increases isavuconazonium sulfate levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Lopinavir and isoflurane both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of ritonavir and lopinavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of isradipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Lopinavir has a similar effect. 24. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of istradefylline by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Do not exceed 20 mg/day of istradefylline when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 25. Itraconazole increases lopinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Ritonavir increases itraconazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ivabradine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 27. Ivacaftor increases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Ritonavir increases ivacaftor levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce ivacaftor dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 28. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ivermectin via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. If the strong inhibitor is discontinued, increase the dose to 500 mg daily after at least five half-lives of the inhibitor. 30. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 31. Ritonavir and ixazomib interactions via CYP3A4 metabolism are minor or of unknown significance. Clinical trials indicate no meaningful change in ixazomib exposure when coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 32. Ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of ketamine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Lopinavir has a similar effect.
